newsitem.title: GREECE: BANK OF GREECE VOWS ANTI-INFLATIONARY STANCE IN '97.
newsitem.headline: BANK OF GREECE VOWS ANTI-INFLATIONARY STANCE IN '97.

text.p: Greece's central bank will maintain its anti-inflationary stance in 1997, targeting ecu/drachma stability, said governor Lucas Papademos during a monetary and forex policy address.
He said the central bank's main goal will be to drive Greece's inflation down to 4.5 percent by the end of the year and below 3.0 percent by year-end 1998.

Greece's foreign exchange policy will stay anti-inflationary but will show greater flexibility this year. The Bank of Greece will take into account inflationary pressures and prevailing conditions in the money and forex markets, he said.

"The policy for the foreign exchange rate of the drachma is defined by the top priority of curbing inflation," Papademos told reporters. "Specifically, the stability of the foreign exchange rate of the drachma against the currencies that make up the ecu will be the main goal of monetary policy."
Greater uncertainty over the relationship between M3 money supply and GDP played a major role in setting the 1997 target range for M3 between 6.0 and 9.0 percent, the same as in 1996, he said.
M3 grew by 9.0 percent at end-96 within the 6-9 percent target zone for the year. M4 monetary aggregate grew by 11.8 percent within the 9.0-12 percent zone.

Total credit growth stood at 5.8 percent at end-96 falling inside the 5-7 percent target range. The central bank set the target range for credit expansion to 4-6 percent in 1997. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
